description: Adjudicated corrections from the September 2026 question audit. 'keep' entries were examined and confirmed sound; they change nothing and are recorded so the audit is complete. Apply with scripts/apply_corrections.py.

judging_criteria.rule: Grade only the claim the question asks for. Wrong volunteered extras (for example a count offered alongside a correct comparison) no longer count against the answer.

Open descriptions accept any fair, grounded description of the scene, not one reference phrasing. 'Also accept:' in an expected answer lists alternates. Not applied to ocr_identification (stays exact) or location_spatial (stays tight).

corrections.question: After panning left 180°, which view has more street lamps—before or after?
corrections.expected_answer: The view after panning left has more street lamps.
corrections.new_expected_answer: The original view has more street lamps.
corrections.rationale: Q_009 asks this at sor-viewpoint and answers 'the original', scoring 39%; Q_001 answers the opposite at 44%. Both cannot hold. The post-turn view measured as a single flat colour, so it contains no lamps.

corrections.question: After a 180 degree turn to the left, which view shows more street lamps – before or after?
corrections.expected_answer: The view after the half-turn shows more buildings.
corrections.new_expected_answer: The original view has more street lamps.
corrections.rationale: The question asks about street lamps and the answer talks about buildings, so the pair does not line up. Aligned rather than retired. The direction is not in doubt: the view after the half-turn has fewer of everything.

corrections.question: Which side of the road has more trees, left or right?
corrections.expected_answer: The left side has more trees.
corrections.rationale: Correct; 43% against the contradicting pair's 11%.

corrections.question: Which side of the road has more trees?
corrections.expected_answer: The Left side has more trees.
corrections.rationale: Correct; same cluster as Q_004.

corrections.question: Which side of the road has more trees, left or right?
corrections.expected_answer: There are no trees on either side of the road
corrections.new_expected_answer: There are more trees on the left side of the road.
corrections.rationale: Q_004 and Q_005 ask the same thing at the same scene and preset and answer 'the left side has more trees'; they score 43%. Q_006 and Q_007 answer 'no trees' and score 11%. Models overwhelmingly report trees, so the 'no trees' pair is the wrong one.

corrections.question: Which side has more trees?
corrections.expected_answer: There are no trees on either side
corrections.new_expected_answer: The left side has more trees.
corrections.rationale: Same claim as Q_006 and the same 11% pass rate. Correcting Q_006 alone would leave the benchmark still asserting both things at once.

corrections.question: After panning left 180 degrees, which view has more street lamps – the original or the after?
corrections.expected_answer: The original view had more street lamps.
corrections.rationale: Correct as written. 39% is genuine model failure, not a grading fault.

corrections.question: After a half-turn, which view shows more buildings—before or after?
corrections.expected_answer: The view after the half-turn shows more buildings.
corrections.new_expected_answer: The view before the half-turn shows more buildings.
corrections.rationale: Q_015 asks this at sor-viewpoint and already answers 'before'. The two contradict; the post-turn view has no buildings in it.

corrections.question: After panning left 180°, which view has more street lamps—before or after?
corrections.expected_answer: The view after panning left has more street lamps.
corrections.new_question: After panning left 180deg, which view has more windows - before or after?
corrections.new_expected_answer: The original view has more windows.
corrections.rationale: Was a verbatim duplicate of Q_001. Rather than drop it, ask about windows instead - the original view has more either way, so the answer holds and the duplication is gone.

corrections.question: After a half-turn, which view shows more buildings—before or after?
corrections.expected_answer: The view before the half-turn shows more buildings
corrections.rationale: Correct as written. 32% is genuine model failure.

corrections.question: Describe the intersection area.
corrections.expected_answer: Two street lamps flank the intersection near the buildings.
corrections.rationale: Reference is fair. Fails on grading, not content - see criteria change C2.

corrections.question: Turn around (pan 180°) and tell me if the road behind you is also wet.
corrections.expected_answer: Yes, the road behind also appears wet.
corrections.new_expected_answer: I don't see a road behind - the view after turning is open sky.
corrections.rationale: Kept, not dropped. whitechapel has geometry on one side only, so the honest answer is that there is no road back there. That makes it a fair test of whether a model reports absence instead of inventing a road.

corrections.question: Turn around (pan 180°) and tell me if the road behind you is also wet.
corrections.expected_answer: Yes, the road behind also appears wet.
corrections.new_expected_answer: I don't see a road behind - the view after turning is open sky.
corrections.rationale: Same fix as Q_098; both kept.

corrections.question: After zooming in on the bike racks, how many bikes do you see?
corrections.expected_answer: I count five bikes.
corrections.rationale: Sound. 4% is genuine counting failure.

corrections.question: Count bikes in the left half of the frame.
corrections.expected_answer: There are about six bikes in the left half
corrections.rationale: Sound. 2% is genuine counting failure.

corrections.question: Go to the store-front preset, then zoom in on the bank sign, then read it out loud.
corrections.expected_answer: I don't see a bank sign in this view.
corrections.new_question: What's the name of the bank by the book nook store?
corrections.rationale: As written it instructs the model to zoom in on a sign and read it, then grades it correct only for reporting the sign is absent. 9% pass across 163 gradings. The instruction and the answer are pulling opposite ways, which is why almost everything fails it.

corrections.question: Zoom in on the bank sign, then read it aloud.
corrections.expected_answer: I have executed the steps in order.
corrections.rationale: Sound as a command-following check.

corrections.question: Is there any graffiti on the Book Nook store?
corrections.expected_answer: No, I don't see any graffiti on the store.
corrections.rationale: Sound.

corrections.question: Across the full view, which are more, trees or street lamps?
corrections.expected_answer: There are more trees than street lamps (8 vs 4).
corrections.new_expected_answer: There are more trees than street lamps.
corrections.rationale: The question asks which is greater; the parenthetical counts invite the judge to demand exact numbers as well, and 90% of answers fail on the counts while getting the comparison right.

corrections.question: Across the full view, how many street lamps are present?
corrections.expected_answer: There are four street lamps.
corrections.rationale: Sound as written. 2% across 163 gradings is genuine model failure: counting over a full 360 view is simply hard, and the question is fair.

corrections.question: Describe what’s in front of the hotel.
corrections.expected_answer: Two garbage cans, a mailbox, and a street lamp stand in front of the hotel.
corrections.rationale: Reference is fair. Fails on grading - see C2.

corrections.question: Describe the sidewalks in this view.
corrections.expected_answer: The sidewalks appear to be made of brick and are well maintained.
corrections.new_expected_answer: Grey rectangular stone slabs. Also accept: concrete.
corrections.rationale: The reference says brick; the sidewalks are stone slabs.

corrections.question: Is there any brand logo visible near the hotel entrance?
corrections.expected_answer: No brand logo is clearly visible near the entrance.
corrections.new_expected_answer: Yes - the sign above the entrance reads “Moonlight”.
corrections.rationale: The sign is legible in the render. Models that said yes were marked wrong.

corrections.question: Describe the town from this vantage point.
corrections.expected_answer: It is a medium-sized town with low-rise buildings, visible barricades, and overgrown areas.
corrections.new_expected_answer: A dense urban area of mixed heights and modern styles - taller buildings with balconies alongside shorter boxy structures, ranging from low-rise blocks to taller towers. Shrubbery and barricades are present.
corrections.rationale: The reference said low-rise; the buildings vary in height, from low-rise blocks to taller towers with balconies. Reference rewritten from the render.

corrections.question: What notable features stand out in the current view?
corrections.expected_answer: Notable features include barricades, rocks, and aged buildings.
corrections.rationale: Reference is fair. Fails on grading - see C2.

corrections.question: Describe the town from this vantage point.
corrections.expected_answer: It is a medium-sized town with low-rise buildings, visible barricades, and overgrown areas.
corrections.new_expected_answer: A dense urban area of mixed heights and modern styles - taller buildings with balconies alongside shorter boxy structures. Shrubbery and barricades are present.
corrections.rationale: Carries Q_462's reference word for word, so it takes the same correction. Kept rather than dropped.
